overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a warm, sunny morning with the running max reaching 69.8°F by 11:45 ET, still well below the NWS forecast high of 75°F with peak heating expected around 14:00–15:30 ET. Short-term velocity is strong (+6.2°F/hr over 30 min) though the 2-hour rate moderates to +2.3°F/hr, suggesting continued but tapering warming into the afternoon. A Heat Advisory is in effect starting Wednesday for inland areas, but today's coastal regime appears more marine-influenced and seasonably mild.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show notable spread: HRRR (76.3°F) and GFS (75.5°F) align with the NWS narrative of ~75°F, while ECMWF (72.1°F) and NBM (70.6°F) print considerably cooler, pulling the ensemble mean toward the low-to-mid 70s. The META model — the most reliable fusion — splits evenly at 45.8% each between the 72–73°F and 74–75°F buckets, reflecting genuine model uncertainty and suggesting the cooler models deserve meaningful weight today.
max_temp_prediction: With approximately 2.5–3.5 hours of heating remaining before the predicted 14:00–15:30 ET peak, and a 2-hour warming rate of +2.3°F/hr from a base of ~69.8°F, a peak in the 73–75°F range appears most probable. The active odd-bucket market's top bucket of 73–74°F (35.1%) aligns well with the META model's center of mass and the ECMWF anchor; confidence is moderate given model spread of ~6°F, but the weight of evidence (META, ECMWF, observed marine influence) leans toward the lower end of the NWS 75°F forecast.
